To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pre-operative Hb and the duration of the surgery are the only factors that can independently predict the requirement for blood transfusion in patients undergoing open prostatectomy.
the pre-operative blood hemoglobin level and duration of the procedure are independent predictors of blood transfusion in patients undergoing open prostatectomy.
a “group and save” policy for patients with pre-operative Hb ≥13.0 gm/dl scheduled for open prostatectomy under spinal anaesthesia is recommended.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors responsible for blood transfusion in the open prostatectomy procedure for BPH.
the determination of factors responsible for perioperative blood transfusion in contemporary open prostatectomy.
the study of the effects of the blood transfusion rate in patients undergoing prostatectomy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a pre-operative Hb ≥13.0 mg/dl, elective surgery, spinal anaesthesia, a short operative duration and a prostate weight of <100 g would reduce the need for peri-operative transfusion in open transvesical prostatectomy for Benign Prostate Hyperplasia (BPH).
a ‘group and save policy’ should be the preferred method of blood ordering for patients with pre-operative Hb of 13.0 gm/dl and above undergoing an open prostatectomy under spinal anaesthesia.
a patient with Hb > 12.0 g/L and a prostate weight < 100 g who is scheduled for elective open prostatectomies under spinal anaesthesia is likely to require blood transfusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a ‘group and save' policy should be the recommended blood ordering procedure for all patients with pre-operative haemoglobin of 13.0 grams per deciliter (g/dl) or higher who are scheduled for an elective prostatectomy under spinal anesthesia, but the need for transfusion may be increased if the operation takes more than 101 minutes.

the pre-operative Hgb level and the duration of the surgery are the most important factors that should be considered when deciding to transfuse peri-operatively in a patient scheduled for open prostatectomy.
blood transfusion in this series of open prostatecomy is mainly determined by the pre-operative HBA1C level and the duration of the procedure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pre-operative anaemia is a strong predictor of peri-operative blood loss and thus blood transfusion in patients undergoing open prostatectomy and that this can be used to guide blood ordering in these patients.

the blood transfusion requirement in open prostatectomies for BPH is not high, and that the pre-operative HBA1C and the duration of the surgery are the only independent predictors of blood transfusion in our setting.
the pre-operative Hbaemia is the most important determinant of blood transfusion in this setting.
